system.summary: Lasry's 'TNA SP106-5' key (Jan 1646): a numerical homophonic alphabet of one- and two-digit values (up to five for E) with a nomenclator written as a letter and a digit (n3 the, k1 of, a1 and, e5 in ...) and a few three-digit numbers; numbers separated by colons.
system.sibling_key: Same key, per Lasry's files, on R928 (ff. 245-246, Dr Stephen Goffe at The Hague, January 1646); also the Charles I-Henrietta Maria key that read rupert1645 (Add MS 72438)
system.notes: Split on 14 Oct 2026 from the former hm1645, which joined six letters in four of Lasry's keys. Lasry's key file says there are no nulls; the figures 81-90, which the key leaves without a value, fall between words, so nulls are left 'unknown' here. Other entries: hm1645 (TNA SP 106 key), sp106r787 (SP106-2), sp106r924 (SP106-8).

solution.what: Fetched the DECODE record page of R929 with the shared cookie; it links Pettersson's transcription, Lasry's reconstructed key 'TNA SP106-5' and his plaintext of ff. 245-247 (2020-10-23).

Applied Lasry's SP106-5 alphabet to Pettersson's raw transcription of f. 247, independently of his plaintext file: it reads English ('... RECEIVED <425>S ... DECEMB ... IANVARY ... THANKES ... WEKLY ADVERTISEMENTS ... CONCERNING THE EMBASSAGE AND MARRIAGE') matching his plaintext.

Re-fetched the record files and applied the key group by group to all 348 groups of f. 247 (apply_key.py): 293 groups get a value, and all 293 equal Lasry's plaintext; 55 groups have no value in the key (17 distinct three-digit numbers, the figures 81-90 between words, e3).

Split from the former combined target hm1645 under the one-key rule (George Lasry, 14 Oct 2026): R929 is the only letter of the six in the SP106-5 key, and the only one where his key was applied here before his plaintext was compared. Folder, profile, page and ledgers separated; earlier steps are kept as recorded.
Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): linked the DECODE record holding Pettersson's transcription and Lasry's plaintext; no local copy

Reading audit, per-document pass (George Lasry's sentence test): Lasry's plaintext of R929 is on DECODE only (git-ignored copy in no checkout); nothing could be read. Relabelled decoded, not read; class already solved kept (Lasry's decipherment); fraction_read 0.842 -> 0.

Re-read (REREAD_BRIEF, b36): DECODE R929 record and all five files fetched with the shared cookie into the session scratchpad (b36_fetch.py): Pettersson's transcription, Lasry's key, interlinear and plaintext files, the image. Neighbours R927, R928, R930 checked: other letters and ciphers, no clear copy of f. 247.

Image rotated and read line by line at full size: ten corrections to the transcription (R929_corrections.tsv): 810 is o2 (twice), 993 is g3, e5 106 is c5 p6, e5 before 'his' is c5, 105 is written p5, and three dates in clear figures. Corrected transcription R929_signs.txt.

o2 = WE (weke, wekly; o0 is WE in the key) adopted at both occurrences; figures 81-90 fall only between words (30 tokens): dividers. Code values from context: 425 your (3), 429 you (2), e3 her (2), 241 King (2); from one context or sense: 334 Queen, 199 give/send, 208 Majesty, 319 Port (+ugall), 259 letter.

Decoded with b36_sp106.py beside Lasry's plaintext (all letter groups agree); reading written in the figures' spelling (R929_reading.md, R929_en.md), aligned word by word with the decode, no supplied words. b17 on the body: 0.273 plain, 0.727 explicit holes (English 1646). Set read, grade B.
Read bar applied per document (v10): 1 of 1 documents marked read measure under 95% of words read as sense (v2_score explicit holes) and are now read in part; read_share recorded for each.

George Lasry gave permission on 24 Oct 2026 to use his DECODE decryptions with attribution: his plaintext file D3083 saved verbatim with an attribution header as lasry/R929_decryption.txt; credit added to R929_reading.md and R929_en.md; read_share re-measured on the reading (v10_relabel.measure); state read in part.

Sibling in the same key: R928 (ff. 245-246, Goffe from The Hague).

texts.label: R929, Paris, 26 Jan 1646
texts.summary: Henrietta Maria's household at Paris to 'Sir', 26 Jan [1646]: the Queen has his letters of 26 Dec and 4 Jan and thanks him for his weekly reports of the King's affairs; however bad they are, the writer hopes they can hold out without further losses until the efforts at Paris for the King's relief take effect; for that, and for the embassy and the Portuguese marriage, he refers him to the King's letters.

reading_review.note: Reading built from the figures with Lasry's key and checked against his decryption on DECODE R929 (D3083, now saved verbatim as lasry/R929_decryption.txt with his permission, 24 Oct 2026); coherent sentences; 566, 554, 620 and the signature codes are the holes.

texts.note: 24 Oct 2026: George Lasry gave permission on 24 Oct 2026 to use his DECODE decryptions with attribution; his plaintext is saved verbatim (lasry/R929_decryption.txt) and credited on the reading and English. read_share measured on R929_reading.md (v10): coherent but under the 95% bar, so read in part; 566, 554, 620 and the signature codes are the holes.
